pos.personaBrief: Inter had 24-33% possession in key ties and Leicester 42.43%, both chose to cede the ball and win by counters (Mourinho: 'win with counters, typical for our team'). Dominance means danger, not possession.

pro.personaBrief: Inter's transitions went instantly to Milito or Eto'o, with long clearances from Julio Cesar; Leicester broke fast through Vardy and Mahrez. Direct, quick play after winning the ball.

est.personaBrief: Compact 4-4-2/4-4-1-1 with two disciplined banks of four and clear roles; little relational fluidity, with Ranieri keeping the same shape in 35 of 38 matches.

lar.personaBrief: Attacks came from fast counters toward forwards and space behind full-backs, not a wing-crossing doctrine. Inter funnelled opponents wide and packed the middle.

blo.personaBrief: Mid/low block, compact lines, dropping off against a team that builds well, and not pressing high; Inter let Barcelona have the ball outside its third and kept a base of four back.

mar.personaBrief: Zonal block with shared responsibility, but Messi was man-marked everywhere and Pandev tucked in to man-mark, so a hybrid that leans zonal with dedicated markers for stars.

pla.personaBrief: Mourinho adapted to Barcelona (refused possession, man-marked Messi, switched to 4-5-1 in-game); Ranieri built around the players' characteristics. Opponent-driven plans and neutralising stronger sides.

res.personaBrief: Result-first: the 10-man Inter's rearguard at 24% possession, settling back once ahead in the final, a negative-minded but winning approach.

sis.personaBrief: Organized, hard-working collectives (aggression, running power, disciplined banks) where everyone defends; Mourinho trusted the system more than individual freedom.

jog.personaBrief: Squads of aggression, hard work, running power; Kante led the league in tackles and interceptions and Vardy's pace was central. Physical intensity over classic technicians.

bas.personaBrief: Inter fielded an experienced side with an average age in the thirties and signed veterans; Leicester kept a settled XI with few changes. Built through signings, not academy.

lid.personaBrief: Mourinho was the firm boss and Ranieri a relaxed man-manager who filtered title talk; both ran a tight, disciplined group where the coach decides.
